Add each subject's conditional distribution of the etas to a fit

Source: R/condDist.R
addCondDist.Rd

Samples each subject's conditional (posterior) distribution of the random effects, `p(eta | y, theta, Omega, sigma)`, at the fit's final population estimates, and stores its mean and SD as `fit$condDist`. It applies to a fit from any mixed-effects estimation method.

Usage

addCondDist(
  fit,
  method = c("auto", "imp", "saem"),
  nsamp = 300L,
  keepSamples = FALSE,
  burn = 50L,
  seed = 42L
)

Arguments

fit

nlmixr2 fit with random effects

method

the sampler: `"auto"` (default) is `"saem"` for a SAEM fit and `"imp"` otherwise

nsamp

number of samples per subject (default 300)

keepSamples

Boolean (default `FALSE`); keep `nsamp` equally weighted draws per subject as the `"samples"` attribute of `fit$condDist`, an `ID x eta x draw` array

burn

MCMC iterations discarded by a held `"saem"` run (default 50)

seed

random seed of the sampler

Value

the fit, with `fit$condDist`: a data frame `ID`, `ETA`, `MEAN`, `SD`. Its `"method"` attribute names the sampler (`"imp"`, `"saem"` for a SAEM fit's own chains or `"mcmc"` for a held SAEM run) and, for `"imp"`, its `"ess"` attribute holds each subject's effective sample size.

Details

`method = "imp"` draws importance samples from a proposal centered at each subject's mode, holding every population parameter at the fit's estimate (the frozen `est = "imp"` E-step), and weights them by the posterior. Mixture, IOV, non-parametric and repeated (`same()`) Omega block fits are not supported.

`method = "saem"` uses the SAEM MCMC kernels. For a SAEM fit, the chains of its own last iterations are the draws when they are enough (`nsamp` draws from `nmc` chains, within the last half of the second-phase iterations, where the parameters have nearly settled), so nothing is simulated; otherwise the kernels run with every population parameter held at the fit's estimates, continuing a SAEM fit's chains or, for any other fit, starting cold, and `burn` iterations are discarded; it needs a model SAEM can fit (every eta on a population parameter of its own). An eta SAEM does not sample for a subject (uninformative) has `SD` `NA` and `MEAN` 0, its prior, as in `fit$eta`; that is exact when the eta is uncorrelated with the others. A model SAEM fits with temporary etas (a likelihood parameter with no eta) is sampled with `"imp"`, since those chains also sampled parameters the reported model holds fixed.

Author

Matthew L. Fidler

Examples

# \donttest{
one.cmt <- function() {
  ini({
    tka <- 0.45
    tcl <- 1
    tv <- 3.45
    eta.ka ~ 0.6
    eta.cl ~ 0.3
    eta.v ~ 0.1
    add.sd <- 0.7
  })
  model({
    ka <- exp(tka + eta.ka)
    cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl)
    v <- exp(tv + eta.v)
    linCmt() ~ add(add.sd)
  })
}
fit <- nlmixr2(one.cmt, nlmixr2data::theo_sd, est = "focei", control = list(print = 0))
